title: Lesson 091 · Fetch–Decode–Execute: A Register Trace
intro: Catch up on the key A Level ideas. Complete four retrieval questions, work through the examples, then practise and explain your reasoning.

questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: Which register holds the current instruction?
Choose the model answer: What is the role of MAR?

Choose the model answer: A full adder has A=1,B=0 and carry-in=1. State Sum and carry-out.

blocks.title: Observe
blocks.text: Fetch copies the address from PC to MAR; memory read transfers the instruction through MDR into CIR. In a sequential fetch, PC advances.

blocks.title: Explain
blocks.text: The Control Unit decodes the current instruction held in CIR and produces the necessary control signals.

blocks.title: Evaluate
blocks.text: Execution of LDA 80 reads the data held at memory address 80 into ACC; the next instruction is not executed until its own fetch.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain the mechanism
blocks.text: Fetch: MAR30, CIR ADD70, PC31. Execution reads memory[70]=5 and ALU adds to ACC4, giving ACC9. The PC increments in fetch while the ALU operates on ACC and fetched operand.

blocks.title: Explain the mechanism
blocks.text: After fetch PC43,CIR SUB90. Operand read from90 into MDR=3; ALU computes11−3, ACC8. The addressed operand must not be confused with instruction address42.
